//factions: Declared by HUE, like the Roman pack: nobody has hand-tuned a palette for
this subject, and core/palette.js keeps the relationship between fill and
wash consistent however many sides there turn out to be.
Six, and the point of six is the coalition. Narvik was retaken by
Norwegian, French, Polish and British troops fighting the same day, and
folding them into one 'allied' colour would hide the one thing about the
land battle a reader should remember. Sweden is `neutral` and stays that
way: the ore is the reason for the whole campaign and never picks a side.

//basemap: No regional Natural Earth extract. The two world levels carry the wide
shots — the North Sea, the ore route down the Baltic — and everything
closer than zoom 9.5 comes from the pack's own OSM detail below. Ofotfjord
is two kilometres wide and Natural Earth at 1:10M does not have it.
//detail: Built by tools/fetch-detail.py from this bbox. The chapters play at zoom
10-12.5, standing on the quay at Narvik, and the whole story is about a
fjord: ten destroyers went up it and could not come out. Without the
pack's own coastline the fjord is not on the map at all.
//borders: Country borders ON, which is the opposite of the two historical packs and
is right here for one reason: the ore is Swedish and the port is
Norwegian, and that border is the whole subject. It is also one of the
oldest unchanged borders in Europe — fixed in 1751 and not moved since —
so drawing today's line across 1940 is honest rather than the

accuracyNote.no: Grensene er dagens. Grensen mellom Norge og Sverige har ligget der siden 1751, men Finland hadde ennå ikke mistet Petsamo, og hadde derfor kyst mot Ishavet.
accuracyNote.en: The borders are the modern ones. The line between Norway and Sweden has stood since 1751, but Finland had not yet lost Petsamo, and so still had a coast on the Arctic Ocean.

//extent: Where this subject's coordinates are allowed to be. The fighting is inside
one fjord, but the story reaches Wilhelmshaven, Scapa Flow, Luleå on the
Baltic and Paris — the campaign was called off because of France, not
because of Narvik. check-data.py uses this to catch a swapped lat/lon.

blurb.no: De kom inn i snøkave og tok byen på tre timer. Så oppdaget de at de ikke hadde nok olje til å komme seg ut igjen.
blurb.en: They came in through a snowstorm and took the town in three hours. Then they found they had not the oil to get out again.

blurb.no: Nordmenn, franskmenn, polakker og briter tok Narvik tilbake den 28. mai. Elleve dager senere seilte de alle sammen bort.
blurb.en: Norwegians, Frenchmen, Poles and Britons took Narvik back on the twenty-eighth of May. Eleven days later all of them sailed away.

//: Where the pixel checks point their camera. s3.b8 is the beat with the whole
of Ofotfjord framed at zoom 9.6 and German markers at Herjangsfjorden,
Ballangen and the harbour — so land, water, place labels and side-coloured
markers are all in the same frame. `at` is 6s because those markers are
anchored to words that land four to six seconds in; sampling earlier finds
an empty fjord and reports it as no data rather than as a fail.
Zoom 9.6 is also above map.detail.minZoom, so this samples the pack's own
OSM coastline rather than Natural Earth. Ofotfjord is two kilometres wide;
at 1:10M there is nothing there to have contrast with.

description.no: Malmen, fjorden og de to sjøslagene – og byen som ble tatt tilbake og forlatt i samme uke.
description.en: The ore, the fjord and the two sea battles – and the town retaken and abandoned in the same week.

generated.//: Photographic-looking generated plates are refused while allowPhoto is false. badge draws the "illustration" mark on every kind:made picture.
